title: Mechanism and Data Driven Grain Condition Information Perception Method for Comprehensive Grain Storage Monitoring
content: Current grain monitoring systems often rely on isolated data points, such as point-based temperature measurements, which limits their ability to assess grain conditions holistically. This study proposes a novel Mechanism and Data Driven (MDD) framework integrating physical mechanisms with real-time sensor data to enable comprehensive grain condition perception. The novel model parameter initialization method achieves high-precision results, demonstrating only a 1.89% error in Day-2 low-temperature zone prediction (27.02 m2 measured vs. 26.52 m2 simulated) and accurately reconstructs temperature fields (≤0.5℃ deviation in YOZ plane) while capturing spatiotemporal dynamics of low-temperature zones. Validation shows superior simulation fidelity (SSIM >0.97 in cloud map comparisons). Compared to the initial values, the simulated total area of low-temperature zones in XOZ plane decreased by 22.97%. Among these, Zone 2 (Center Area) showed a 25.30% reduction, while Zone 1 (near the south exterior wall) exhibited a more substantial decline of 27.64%, higher than the 20.35% reduction in Zone 3. High-temperature zones exhibit low moisture content, whereas low-temperature zones retain elevated moisture levels (>14%). A strong positive correlation exists between relative humidity and temperature fields. As the temperature field progressively homogenizes, it induces corresponding uniformity in humidity distribution. The proposed framework provides a comprehensive approach to grain condition monitoring, delivering both holistic insights and actionable data for smart ventilation control, early condensation risk warnings, and mold prevention. It establishes a robust data foundation and practical methodologies for intelligent storage management, ultimately reducing post-harvest grain.
